name: Sigmund Freud
kicker: Founder of psychoanalysis · Mapped the mind’s hidden, unconscious side
briefing: Sigmund Freud believed that dreams, slips of the tongue, and even jokes were secret messages from a hidden part of the mind he called the unconscious. This Austrian doctor spent his career in Vienna listening to patients and built an entirely new way to treat the mind called psychoanalysis. His ideas about the id, the ego, and the superego still shape how people talk about personality today.

tossups.p: Born Sigismund Schlomo in a town now part of the Czech Republic, this man trained as a Vienna neurologist and co-wrote _Studies on Hysteria_ with Josef Breuer [“BROY-er”]. He argued that a death drive called Thanatos [“THAN-uh-tahss”] opposes the life-seeking drive Eros in his book _Beyond the Pleasure Principle_.
tossups.r: His case studies included “Dora” and a boy called “Little Hans.” This thinker split the mind into the id, the ego, and the superego, and claimed in _The Interpretation of Dreams_ that dreams reveal hidden wishes. For 10 points, name this Austrian founder of psychoanalysis.

tossups.p: This thinker’s patient “Little Hans” and his fear of horses became a famous case study, later used to illustrate the Oedipus complex, one of this man’s best-known ideas. In _Totem and Taboo_, he applied his theories to the origins of religion and society, and _Moses and Monotheism_ controversially argued that a biblical figure had followed the pharaoh Akhenaten [“AH-ken-AH-ten”].
tossups.r: He trained under Josef Breuer in Vienna and later clashed with former followers Carl Jung and Alfred Adler. This thinker proposed that the mind has three parts: the id, the ego, and the superego. For 10 points, name this Austrian psychoanalyst who wrote _The Interpretation of Dreams_.

tossups.p: In _The Future of an Illusion_, this thinker argued that religious belief grows out of deep psychological needs, and in _Civilization and Its Discontents_, he claimed that society’s rules create constant inner tension. His book _Jokes and Their Relation to the Unconscious_ explored why people find things funny.
tossups.r: He proposed that a death drive called Thanatos opposes the life-seeking drive Eros in _Beyond the Pleasure Principle_. This thinker divided the mind into the id, the ego, and the superego. For 10 points, name this founder of psychoanalysis, who wrote _The Interpretation of Dreams_.

tossups.p: This man fled Nazi-occupied Vienna for London in 1938, years after the Nazis burned his books; his daughter Anna, who became a respected psychoanalyst herself, had already been questioned by the Gestapo [“guh-SHTAH-poh”]. Early followers Carl Jung, Alfred Adler, and Otto Rank each eventually broke away from this thinker’s ideas.
tossups.r: He analyzed a dream he called “Irma’s Injection” to argue that dreams express hidden wishes. This thinker split the mind into the id, the ego, and the superego. For 10 points, name this Austrian founder of psychoanalysis, the author of _The Interpretation of Dreams_.

tossups.p: In _The Ego and the Id_, this thinker fully laid out his three-part model of the mind, building on ideas he had introduced in _Beyond the Pleasure Principle_. That earlier book contrasted a death drive called Thanatos with a life-seeking drive called Eros.
tossups.r: His case studies included a young woman known as “Dora” and a boy called “Little Hans.” This thinker proposed that people have an unconscious mind full of hidden thoughts, and that the mind divides into the id, the ego, and the superego. For 10 points, name this Austrian founder of psychoanalysis.

tossups.p: Working alongside his early mentor Josef Breuer, this man co-wrote _Studies on Hysteria_, an early step toward the treatment he later named psychoanalysis. He proposed the Oedipus complex as one of his central ideas about childhood development.

clues.t: Founded psychoanalysis, a way of treating the mind by talking through hidden thoughts and feelings
Wrote _The Interpretation of Dreams_ (1900), arguing that dreams reveal hidden wishes
Divided the mind into three parts: the id, the ego, and the superego
Believed a hidden unconscious mind, below conscious awareness, drives much of human behavior
Austrian doctor who spent most of his career treating patients in Vienna
Proposed the Oedipus complex, one of his best-known and most debated ideas about childhood
In _Beyond the Pleasure Principle_, contrasted the death drive Thanatos with the life-seeking drive Eros
Pioneered “talk therapy”: having patients freely say whatever came to mind (free association)
_Civilization and Its Discontents_ argued that society’s rules create constant inner tension
Case study of a boy called “Little Hans” examined a young child’s fear of horses
“Irma’s Injection” was his own dream, which he analyzed to argue that dreams fulfill secret wishes
Early followers Carl Jung, Alfred Adler, and Otto Rank each eventually broke away from his ideas
_The Ego and the Id_ (1923) laid out his three-part model of the mind in full
_Moses and Monotheism_ controversially claimed Moses had been a follower of the pharaoh Akhenaten
_Totem and Taboo_ applied his psychological theories to the origins of religion and society
_The Future of an Illusion_ argued that religious belief grows out of deep psychological need
His book _Jokes and Their Relation to the Unconscious_ studied why people find things funny
Famous case studies included “Dora” and the “Wolf Man”; “Anna O.” was really his mentor Breuer’s patient
With mentor Josef Breuer, co-wrote _Studies on Hysteria_ (1895), an early step toward psychoanalysis
Fled Austria for London in 1938 after the Nazi takeover; his daughter Anna had been questioned by the Gestapo
Born Sigismund Schlomo in 1856, in a Moravian town now part of the Czech Republic

trap.title: Father, not daughter
trap.body: Sigmund Freud’s daughter, Anna Freud, became a respected psychoanalyst in her own right, and clues sometimes mention her, such as her questioning by the Gestapo as the family fled the Nazis. Early clues also often name Carl Jung, Alfred Adler, or Otto Rank, three early followers of Freud who later broke away from his ideas.
trap.fix: If a clue says “his daughter” or describes a follower of this man who later disagreed with him, the answer is still the father, not the other name in the sentence. Save “Jung,” “Adler,” or “Rank” for a tossup that actually asks about them.
trap.line: Real answer line: Sigmund Freud (prompt on Sigmund; accept Sigismund Schlomo Freud)
